summary: The documentation updates the worktree and PIT routes coherently, but the focused PIT examples do not actually guarantee per-run evidence isolation.

findings.title: Timestamped focused PIT directory can be reused
findings.trigger: A successful focused run and a retry with the same label begin within the same UTC second, and the retry fails before producing mutations.xml.
findings.consequence: The retry reuses the prior directory and leaves its archived mutations.xml in place, so a later audit or ledger entry can treat stale XML as evidence for the failed retry.
findings.evidence: verification/pit.md:66 creates a name with only second precision and uses mkdir -p, which accepts an existing directory. The generic example repeats this at verification/pit.md:101. When the retry produces no report, the conditional copies at lines 73 and 108 do not remove an existing archived mutations.xml, contradicting the per-run requirement at lines 138-140.
findings.suggestedFix: Create the evidence directory with a collision-resistant temporary-directory mechanism, require creation to fail when the path already exists, and apply the same behavior to both focused-run examples.
